original_value: By using the high spectral resolution, hyperspectral images (HSIs) provide significant information for target detection, which is of great interest in HSI processing. However, most classical target detection methods may only perform well based on certain assumptions. Simultaneously, using limited numbers of target samples and preserving the discriminative information is also a challenging problem in hyperspectral target detection. To overcome these shortcomings, this paper proposes a novel adaptive information-theoretic metric learning with local constraints (ITML-ALC) for hyperspectral target detection. The proposed method firstly uses the information-theoretic metric learning (ITML) method as the objective function for learning a Mahalanobis distance to separate similar and dissimilar point-pairs without certain assumptions, needing fewer adjusted parameters. Then, adaptively local constraints are applied to shrink the distances between samples of similar pairs and expand the distances between samples of dissimilar pairs. Finally, target detection decision can be made by considering both the threshold and the changes between the distances before and after metric learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can obviously separate target samples from background ones and outperform both the state-of-the-art target detection algorithms and the other classical metric learning methods.

result.paraphrase: Leveraging high spectral resolution, hyperspectral images (HSIs) contain rich information for target detection, a key task in HSI processing. Yet most traditional target detection methods work well only under specific assumptions, and hyperspectral target detection also faces the challenge of using limited target samples while retaining discriminative information. To address these issues, this paper presents a new adaptive information-theoretic metric learning with local constraints (ITML-ALC) approach for hyperspectral target detection. First, it adopts information-theoretic metric learning (ITML) as the objective function to learn a Mahalanobis distance that separates similar and dissimilar point pairs without relying on particular assumptions and with fewer tuning parameters. Next, adaptive local constraints are introduced to reduce the distances of similar pairs and increase those of dissimilar pairs. Finally, target detection decisions are made by taking into account both the threshold and the distance changes before and after metric learning. Experimental results show that the proposed method can clearly distinguish target samples from background samples and outperform state-of-the-art target detection algorithms as well as other classical metric learning methods.
